title: Command (verb) display and rhythmic intermission
description: The single giant imperative verb shown at microgame start, plus the cognitive-buffer intermission between microgames, hooked into the sequencer lifecycle. Follows unity-microgame-framework and the GDD UI guidance.
acceptance_criteria: A command display shows one large, high-legibility imperative verb (e.g. '¡ESQUIVA!') at microgame start for roughly one second.
An intermission screen plays between microgames as a cognitive buffer with a configurable duration.
Intermission timing is testable in pure C# (a timer/state machine separate from rendering).
Both are driven by the sequencer lifecycle, not hardcoded per microgame.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: Done. RoundPhaseMachine (Barcade.Core/Loop): Intermission->CommandShow(~1s)->Play(seq effective duration)->Result; configurable durations, negative clamped, deterministic, zero-duration lazy-drain on Tick; PhaseChangedThisTick/VerbText/IsRoundComplete. 138/138 fast tests. Framework views (CommandDisplayView, IntermissionView, MicrogameLoopController) written, compile deferred to Unity integration pass. Test d5e47e8, impl 28f41fd. Reviewer APPROVED no HIGH. CARRY-FORWARD to TASK-015 (must-fix): (1) MicrogameLoopController fires OnRoundComplete the instant IsRoundComplete -> Result window/_resultDuration skipped; fix by timing Result in the controller OR have the machine make Result a timed phase exposing ResultComplete; (2) lock the zero-duration lazy-drain contract (review noted impl adjusted some tests to match code); (3) wire real per-player bool[4] results (currently stubbed) and Play/Result view branches. Framework files needing integration compile: CommandDisplayView.cs, IntermissionView.cs, MicrogameLoopController.cs.
